liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **China Doll** (2 reviews): Reviewer says China Doll alone would have satisfied the audience; The harmonies on China Doll stand out [6][9]
- **Black Throated Wind** (1 review): Black Throated Wind carries real emotional weight [9]
- **Eyes Of The World** (1 review): Eyes Of The World features strong, hard-hitting jamming [9]
- **Loose Lucy** (1 review): Loose Lucy is played in the old-school style, which the reviewer values [6]
- **Weather Report Suite** (1 review): Reviewer calls this the best Weather Report Suite they have heard, praising Phil's bass lines [7]
- **Let It Grow** (1 review): A rare Let It Grow jam leads into The Other One in a mind-bending sequence [12]
- **Morning Dew** (1 review): Encore Morning Dew is sparse, with bass, piano and drums giving it a canyon-like spaciousness and Garcia vocal inflections; After the verses comes a very extended, tender quiet stretch, then Garcia's buzzsaw tone at 12:05 and a long crescendo [11]
- **It's A Sin** (1 review): It's A Sin is regrettably short, followed by a soulful Stella Blue [12]

## Setlist highlights

- **It's A Sin Jam**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [17]

## The recordings

- **gd1974-06-18.sbd.pitch-fixed-sacks.32528.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 22 songs; 177 min; rated 5/5 by 8 [1]
- **gd74-06-18.sbd.sacks.209.sbefail.shnf**: soundboard; 22 songs; 174 min; rated 4.59/5 by 81 [2]. Said about its sound: The CD copy is very clean compared with the old cassette the reviewer knew; Sound quality is crisp and bright; Described as a newly circulating crisp version; disc 3 track 2 had a flaw that was fixed [2][7][14]
- **gd1974-06-18.sbd.bertha-ashley.18150.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 23 songs; 174 min; rated 4.36/5 by 11 [3]. Said about its sound: Major mix problems affect the first three set-one tracks; the original is slightly overdriven, causing minor crackling [3]
- **gd1974-06-18.sbd.miller.89690.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 21 songs; 176 min; rated 4.3/5 by 23 [4]

## Around the show

- Reviewer in Ames recalls a long, loud show with thunderstorm and rain; band played under an awning and cut the electrics [8]
- After the storm a large rainbow appeared over the stage, like the Europe 72 cover [8]
- The show was held indoors at Freedom Hall, so thunderstorms there would be surprising [10]
- Some listeners rank this the best show of 1974 [5]
- For The Other One, ranks near the 9/17/72 version, though shorter [12]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1974-06-18.sbd.pitch-fixed-sacks.32528.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by JoshD; source: SPEED-CORRECTED VERSION of SBD>MR>1 cass>DAT>ZA2>SHN [1]. Also: Speed was corrected by -28 cents in Cool Edit Pro, with pitch judged against a guitar tuned to A=440; The original source tracked Loose Lucy at the end of disc 1; it was moved to disc 2 [1]
- **gd74-06-18.sbd.sacks.209.sbefail.shnf**: source: Soundboard [2]. Also: Reviewer's own copy of the show passed from cassette to DAT to CD over the years; Chain: soundboard to MR to one cassette to DAT to ZA2 to SHN, via D. Sacks and D. Hollister [2][6]
- **gd1974-06-18.sbd.bertha-ashley.18150.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Jay Ashley; source: SBD>>MR>>DAT>>ZA2>>SHN>>DAW(Bertha) [3]. Also: Remastered January 12, 2003 by an archive.org user on a dual-DAW system nicknamed Bertha; source from Darrin Sacks, David Hollister [3]
- **gd1974-06-18.sbd.miller.89690.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Cassette -> Dat -> SHN -> Cool Edit Pro -> CD [4]. Also: Remaster of shnid 32528 with levels adjusted, DC offset removed and minor cleanup [4]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Freedom Hall - June 18, 1974](https://www.dead.net/show/june-18-1974) [18]
